'''Alan Cyril Walker''' (23 August 1938 – 20 November 2017)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mnsu.edu/emuseum/information/biography/uvwxyz/walker_alan.html |title=Alan Walker |access-date=22 June 2005 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050420044035/http://www.mnsu.edu/emuseum/information/biography/uvwxyz/walker_alan.html |archive-date=20 April 2005 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ncse.com/news/2017/11/alan-walker-dies-0018658 |title=Alan Walker dies |website=NCSE |access-date=23 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.psu.edu/story/495615/2017/11/22/research/penn-state-mourns-passing-alan-walker |title=Penn State mourns passing of Alan Walker |access-date=6 October 2019}}</ref> was the [[Evan Pugh Professor]] of [[Biological Anthropology]] and Biology at the [[Pennsylvania State University]] and a research scientist for the [[National Museum of Kenya]].<ref name="88Macarthur">{{Cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1988/07/19/us/macarthur-foundation-names-31-recipients-of-1988-awards.html |title=MacArthur Foundation Names 31 Recipients of 1988 Awards |last=Teltsch |first=Kathleen |date=19 July 1988 |website=The New York Times |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170924185541/http://www.nytimes.com/1988/07/19/us/macarthur-foundation-names-31-recipients-of-1988-awards.html |archive-date=2017-09-24 |access-date=22 November 2017}}</ref>

== Life ==
He received his B.A. from Cambridge University in 1962, and his PhD from the University of London in 1967.  In 2000 he received an honorary D.Sc. from the University of Chicago.<ref name="Uchicago">{{Cite web |url=https://convocation.uchicago.edu/page/2000 |title=Honorary Degrees 2000–2009 |publisher=University of Chicago |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808032536/https://convocation.uchicago.edu/page/2000 |archive-date=2017-08-08 |access-date=22 November 2017}}</ref>

Walker was a paleoanthropologist who worked on primate and human evolution.<ref>[http://www.anthro.psu.edu/faculty_staff/walker.shtml Alan Walker's page at Pennsylvania State University] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070812233023/http://www.anthro.psu.edu/faculty_staff/walker.shtml |date=12 August 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hlusko |first1=Leslea J. |last2=Ungar |first2=Peter S. |date=2019-08-21 |title=Alan Cyril Walker. 23 August 1938—20 November 2017 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=67 |pages=449–467 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2019.0017|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Walker was a member of the team led by [[Richard Leakey]] responsible for the 1984 discovery of the skeleton of the so-called [[Turkana Boy]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sn/prehistoric_life/human/human_evolution/leaving_home1.shtml |title=Leaving home – 2 million years ago |date=17 September 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171001205519/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sn/prehistoric_life/human/human_evolution/leaving_home1.shtml |archive-date=2017-10-01 |url-status=live |access-date=25 November 2017}}</ref> and in 1985 Walker himself discovered the [[Black Skull]]<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.archaeologyinfo.com/australopithecusaethiopicus.htm | title=Australopithecus aethiopicus - A Robust Australopithecine | access-date=16 February 2011 | archive-date=16 May 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110516121312/http://www.archaeologyinfo.com/australopithecusaethiopicus.htm | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/the-top-seven-human-evolution-discoveries-in-kenya-69297642/ |title=The Top Seven Human Evolution Discoveries in Kenya |last=Wayman |first=Erin |date=18 April 2012 |website=Smithsonian.com |access-date=22 November 2017}}</ref> near [[Lake Turkana]] in Kenya.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hlusko|first1=Leslea J.|last2=Ungar|first2=Peter S.|date=2019-12-30|title=Alan Cyril Walker. 23 August 1938—20 November 2017|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=67|pages=449–467|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2019.0017|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Awards==
Walker was awarded a [[MacArthur Fellowship]] "genius grant" in 1988.<ref>{{cite web
 |url         = http://www.macfound.org/site/c.lkLXJ8MQKrH/b.1142699/k.7B86/Fellows_List__August_1988.htm
 |title       = Fellows List – August 1988
 |publisher   = [[MacArthur Foundation]]
 |access-date  = 7 December 2006
 |url-status     = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20100212081433/http://www.macfound.org/site/c.lkLXJ8MQKrH/b.1142699/k.7B86/Fellows_List__August_1988.htm
 |archive-date = 12 February 2010
}}</ref><ref name="88Macarthur" /> 
In 1997 he received the Rhône-Poulenc Award from the [[Royal Society]] for ''The Wisdom of the Bones'' co-authored with Pat Shipman.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shipman, Pat 1949– {{!}} Encyclopedia.com |url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/arts/educational-magazines/shipman-pat-1949 |access-date=2025-06-18 |website=www.encyclopedia.com}}</ref> During the award ceremony, [[Terry Pratchett]], chairman of the judges, said "We were fascinated by the way the forensic net was spread out, bringing so many sciences to bear on the mystery of this million-year-old teenager."  The following year he received the [[International Prize (Fyssen Foundation)|International Fondation Fyssen Prize]] in Paris.<ref name="fyssen">{{Cite web  |url=http://www.fondation-fyssen.org/prixUS.html  |title=International Prize  |access-date=22 November 2017  |archive-date=21 February 2014  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221205729/http://www.fondation-fyssen.org/prixUS.html  |url-status=dead  }}</ref>

Walker and Shipman also co-wrote ''The Ape in the Tree'', published in 2005, describing the history of discovery and scientific investigation of the ''[[Proconsul (mammal)|Proconsul]]'' fossils in Kenya.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Walker |first1=Alan |title=The ape in the tree: an intellectual & natural history of Proconsul |last2=Shipman |first2=Pat |date=2005 |publisher=Belknap Press of Harvard Univ. Press |isbn=978-0-674-01675-0 |location=Cambridge, Mass.}}</ref> 

He was elected as a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1996,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www8.nationalacademies.org/onpinews/newsitem.aspx?RecordID=12825 |title=Members of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences in the Eberly College of Science |publisher=Pennsylvania State University |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170210182950/http://www8.nationalacademies.org/onpinews/newsitem.aspx?RecordID=12825 |archive-date=2017-02-10 |access-date=22 November 2017}}</ref> and as a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1999.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/alan-walker-12472/|title=Alan Walker Biography|publisher= Royal Society|access-date= 16 January 2017}}</ref> In 2003 he was named a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite press release |title=National Academy of Science |url=http://www8.nationalacademies.org/onpinews/newsitem.aspx?RecordID=12825}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/alan-walker-honouo/ |title=Member Directory |website=National Academy of Science |access-date=22 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160718222604/http://www.nasonline.org/member-directory/members/20004896.html |archive-date=18 July 2016 |url-status=live |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

In 2017 he received the Charles R. Darwin Lifetime Achievement Award from the [[American Association of Biological Anthropologists]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Charles R. Darwin Lifetime Achievement Award |url=https://bioanth.org/about/the-charles-r-darwin-lifetime-achievement-award/ |access-date=2025-06-18 |website=AABA |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Bibliography==
* 1996 (with his wife Pat Shipman). ''The Wisdom of Bones''. Weidenfeld & Nicolson, London.
* 1993 (with [[Richard Leakey]]) eds. ''The Nariokotome Homo erectus Skeleton''. Cambridge MA: Harvard University Press. 
* 1997 (with [[Meave Leakey]]). ''Early Hominid Fossils from Africa''. [[Scientific American]] '''276''', 6, 74–79 [http://www.nature.com/scientificamerican/journal/v276/n6/pdf/scientificamerican0697-74.pdf?foxtrotcallback=true]
* 2005. ''The Ape in the Tree: An Intellectual and Natural History of Proconsul''. The Belknap Press of Harvard UP, Cambridge, Mass.
